from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from core.apikeys import ApiKeyRecord, KeyScope, KeyStatus, registry
from core.auth import AuthPrincipal, require_scope, resolve_api_key


router = APIRouter(prefix="/customerkeys", tags=["customer-keys"])

CustomerKeyStatus = Literal["active", "revoked"]


def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


class CustomerApiKeyCreateRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=200)
    owner_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Optional owner identifier. Defaults to the authenticated principal subject.",
    )


class CustomerApiKeyResponse(BaseModel):
    key_id: str
    name: str
    key_prefix: str
    key_hint: str
    scope: KeyScope
    status: KeyStatus
    owner_id: str | None = None
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str
    last_used_at: str | None = None
    revoked_at: str | None = None
    # Only returned on creation/rotation
    raw_key: str | None = None


class CustomerApiKeyListResponse(BaseModel):
    items: list[CustomerApiKeyResponse] = Field(default_factory=list)


class CustomerApiKeyRotateResponse(BaseModel):
    key_id: str
    name: str
    key_prefix: str
    key_hint: str
    scope: KeyScope
    status: KeyStatus
    owner_id: str | None = None
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str
    last_used_at: str | None = None
    revoked_at: str | None = None
    raw_key: str


def _to_response(record: ApiKeyRecord, raw_key: str | None = None) -> CustomerApiKeyResponse:
    return CustomerApiKeyResponse(
        key_id=record.key_id,
        name=record.name,
        key_prefix=record.key_prefix,
        key_hint=record.key_hint,
        scope=record.scope,
        status=record.status,
        owner_id=record.owner_id,
        created_at=record.created_at,
        updated_at=record.updated_at,
        last_used_at=record.last_used_at,
        revoked_at=record.revoked_at,
        raw_key=raw_key,
    )


@router.get("", response_model=CustomerApiKeyListResponse)
def list_customer_keys(
    principal: AuthPrincipal = Depends(resolve_api_key),
) -> CustomerApiKeyListResponse:
    # Only customer or system principals can list customer keys
    require_scope(principal, "customer", "internal")

    records = registry.list_keys(
        owner_id=principal.subject,
        scope="customer",
    )
    items = [_to_response(r) for r in records]
    return CustomerApiKeyListResponse(items=items)


@router.post(
    "",
    response_model=CustomerApiKeyResponse,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
)
def create_customer_key(
    body: CustomerApiKeyCreateRequest,
    principal: AuthPrincipal = Depends(resolve_api_key),
) -> CustomerApiKeyResponse:
    # Customers can only create keys for themselves; internal/system can override owner_id
    if principal.principal_type == "customer":
        owner_id = principal.subject
    else:
        owner_id = body.owner_id or principal.subject

    require_scope(principal, "customer", "internal")

    record, raw_key = registry.create_key(
        name=body.name,
        scope="customer",
        owner_id=owner_id,
        prefix="icpk",
    )
    return _to_response(record, raw_key=raw_key)


@router.post(
    "/{key_id}/rotate",
    response_model=CustomerApiKeyRotateResponse,
)
def rotate_customer_key(
    key_id: str,
    principal: AuthPrincipal = Depends(resolve_api_key),
) -> CustomerApiKeyRotateResponse:
    require_scope(principal, "customer", "internal")

    record = registry.get_key(key_id)
    if record is None or record.scope != "customer":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail="Customer API key not found",
        )

    if principal.principal_type == "customer" and record.owner_id != principal.subject:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Not allowed to rotate this API key",
        )

    rotated, raw_key = registry.rotate_key(key_id=key_id, prefix="icpk")

    return CustomerApiKeyRotateResponse(
        key_id=rotated.key_id,
        name=rotated.name,
        key_prefix=rotated.key_prefix,
        key_hint=rotated.key_hint,
        scope=rotated.scope,
        status=rotated.status,
        owner_id=rotated.owner_id,
        created_at=rotated.created_at,
        updated_at=rotated.updated_at,
        last_used_at=rotated.last_used_at,
        revoked_at=rotated.revoked_at,
        raw_key=raw_key,
    )


@router.post(
    "/{key_id}/revoke",
    response_model=CustomerApiKeyResponse,
)
def revoke_customer_key(
    key_id: str,
    principal: AuthPrincipal = Depends(resolve_api_key),
) -> CustomerApiKeyResponse:
    require_scope(principal, "customer", "internal")

    record = registry.get_key(key_id)
    if record is None or record.scope != "customer":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail="Customer API key not found",
        )

    if principal.principal_type == "customer" and record.owner_id != principal.subject:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Not allowed to revoke this API key",
        )

    if record.status == "revoked":
        # Idempotent revoke; just return existing record
        return _to_response(record)

    now = _utc_now_iso()
    record.status = "revoked"
    record.revoked_at = now
    record.updated_at = now

    return _to_response(record)


@router.get(
    "/{key_id}",
    response_model=CustomerApiKeyResponse,
)
def get_customer_key(
    key_id: str,
    principal: AuthPrincipal = Depends(resolve_api_key),
) -> CustomerApiKeyResponse:
    require_scope(principal, "customer", "internal")

    record = registry.get_key(key_id)
    if record is None or record.scope != "customer":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail="Customer API key not found",
        )

    if principal.principal_type == "customer" and record.owner_id != principal.subject:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Not allowed to view this API key",
        )

    return _to_response(record)

FILE: api\execute.py

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from services.securityorchestrator import (
    SecurityOrchestratorService,
    build_security_orchestration_request,
)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/execute", tags=["execute"])

_service = SecurityOrchestratorService()


class ExecuteRequest(BaseModel):
    request_id: str | None = Field(default=None)
    action: str = Field(default="execute", min_length=1)
    target: str = Field(default="runtime", min_length=1)
    payload: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    risk_score: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, le=100)
    source: str | None = None
    actor_id: str | None = None
    session_id: str | None = None
    organization_id: str | None = None
    requires_network: bool = False
    requires_filesystem: bool = False
    requires_secrets: bool = False
    requires_human_review: bool = False
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)


class ExecuteResponse(BaseModel):
    record_id: str
    request_id: str
    status: str
    outcome: str
    allowed: bool
    orchestration: dict[str, Any]
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str | None = None


@router.post("", response_model=ExecuteResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
def execute(request: ExecuteRequest) -> ExecuteResponse:
    orchestration_request = build_security_orchestration_request(
        request_id=request.request_id,
        action=request.action,
        target=request.target,
        payload=request.payload,
        risk_score=request.risk_score,
        source=request.source,
        actor_id=request.actor_id,
        session_id=request.session_id,
        organization_id=request.organization_id,
        requires_network=request.requires_network,
        requires_filesystem=request.requires_filesystem,
        requires_secrets=request.requires_secrets,
        requires_human_review=request.requires_human_review,
        metadata=request.metadata,
    )
    record = _service.execute(orchestration_request)
    return ExecuteResponse.model_validate(record.to_dict())


@router.get("/{record_id}", response_model=ExecuteResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
def get_execution(record_id: str) -> ExecuteResponse:
    record = _service.get_record(record_id)
    if record is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail=f"Execution record '{record_id}' was not found.",
        )
    return ExecuteResponse.model_validate(record.to_dict())


@router.get("", response_model=list[ExecuteResponse], status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
def list_executions() -> list[ExecuteResponse]:
    return [ExecuteResponse.model_validate(item) for item in _service.list_records_dict()]


__all__ = [
    "ExecuteRequest",
    "ExecuteResponse",
    "router",
]

FILE: api\routes\release_policy.py
================================================================================
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from hashlib import sha256
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


router = APIRouter(
    prefix="/release-policy",
    tags=["release-policy"],
)


class ReleasePolicySummary(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    policy_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=64)
    version: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=32)
    channel: Literal["dev", "staging", "production"]
    status: Literal["active", "draft", "deprecated"]
    minimum_upgrade_from: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=32)
    backup_required: bool
    migration_required: bool
    rollout_strategy: Literal["manual", "canary", "blue-green", "in-place"]


class ReleasePolicyDetail(ReleasePolicySummary):
    generated_at: datetime
    checksum: str = Field(min_length=64, max_length=64)
    compatibility_notes: list[str]
    required_env: list[str]
    preflight_checks: list[str]
    upgrade_steps: list[str]
    rollback_steps: list[str]


class ReleasePolicyListResponse(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    items: list[ReleasePolicySummary]
    count: int


def _utcnow() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


def _build_policy(
    *,
    version: str,
    channel: Literal["dev", "staging", "production"],
) -> ReleasePolicyDetail:
    generated_at = _utcnow()

    compatibility_notes = [
        "Use verified environment files before deployment.",
        "Run deployment readiness and smoke verification before cutover.",
        "Do not skip backup generation before restore-impacting upgrades.",
    ]
    required_env = [
        "IRONCLAW_ENV",
        "IRONCLAW_BASE_URL",
        "SUPABASE_URL",
        "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY",
    ]
    preflight_checks = [
        "python -m scripts.verify",
        "python -m scripts.securityqualitygate",
        "python -m scripts.deploymentreadiness",
        "python -m scripts.smoketest --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000",
    ]
    upgrade_steps = [
        "Create backup snapshot.",
        "Validate environment configuration.",
        "Build updated container image.",
        "Apply deployment compose changes.",
        "Run readiness and smoke verification.",
    ]
    rollback_steps = [
        "Stop failed rollout.",
        "Restore previous image and compose state.",
        "Run restore flow from latest verified backup if data regression is detected.",
        "Re-run smoke verification.",
    ]

    checksum_source = "|".join(
        [
            version,
            channel,
            "active",
            ",".join(required_env),
            ",".join(preflight_checks),
            ",".join(upgrade_steps),
            ",".join(rollback_steps),
        ]
    )

    return ReleasePolicyDetail(
        policy_id=f"ironclaw-{channel}",
        version=version,
        channel=channel,
        status="active",
        minimum_upgrade_from="1.0.0",
        backup_required=True,
        migration_required=channel in {"staging", "production"},
        rollout_strategy="blue-green" if channel == "production" else "canary",
        generated_at=generated_at,
        checksum=sha256(checksum_source.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
        compatibility_notes=compatibility_notes,
        required_env=required_env,
        preflight_checks=preflight_checks,
        upgrade_steps=upgrade_steps,
        rollback_steps=rollback_steps,
    )


def _policy_catalog() -> dict[str, ReleasePolicyDetail]:
    return {
        "dev": _build_policy(version="1.0.0-dev", channel="dev"),
        "staging": _build_policy(version="1.0.0-rc1", channel="staging"),
        "production": _build_policy(version="1.0.0", channel="production"),
    }


@router.get(
    "",
    response_model=ReleasePolicyListResponse,
    summary="List release policies",
)
def list_release_policies(
    channel: Annotated[
        Literal["dev", "staging", "production"] | None,
        Query(
            description="Optionally filter release policies by channel.",
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> ReleasePolicyListResponse:
    catalog = _policy_catalog()
    items = list(catalog.values())

    if channel is not None:
        items = [policy for policy in items if policy.channel == channel]

    summaries = [
        ReleasePolicySummary.model_validate(policy.model_dump())
        for policy in items
    ]
    return ReleasePolicyListResponse(items=summaries, count=len(summaries))


@router.get(
    "/{channel}",
    response_model=ReleasePolicyDetail,
    summary="Get release policy by channel",
)
def get_release_policy(
    channel: Literal["dev", "staging", "production"],
) -> ReleasePolicyDetail:
    policy = _policy_catalog().get(channel)
    if policy is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="release policy not found")
    return policy

"""IronClaw application package."""

================================================================================
FILE: app\adapters\base.py

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

from app.services.adapter_manifest import AdapterManifest, build_adapter_manifest
from app.services.integration_registry import IntegrationRecord


AdapterHealth = Literal["ready", "degraded", "offline"]
AdapterExecutionStatus = Literal[
    "accepted",
    "accepted_with_warnings",
    "guarded",
    "blocked",
    "offline",
    "failed",
]


def _utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _normalize_text(value: str | None) -> str:
    return (value or "").strip()


def _clean_dict(value: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return dict(value or {})


def _clean_list_of_dicts(value: list[dict[str, Any]] | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not value:
        return []
    return [dict(item) for item in value]


def _require_text(value: str | None, field_name: str) -> str:
    normalized = _normalize_text(value)
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} is required")
    return normalized


@dataclass(slots=True)
class AdapterHandshake:
    adapter_slug: str
    platform: str
    protocol_version: str
    status: AdapterHealth
    connected_at: str
    capabilities: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.adapter_slug = _require_text(self.adapter_slug, "adapter_slug")
        self.platform = _require_text(self.platform, "platform")
        self.protocol_version = _require_text(self.protocol_version, "protocol_version")
        self.connected_at = _require_text(self.connected_at, "connected_at")
        self.capabilities = _clean_list_of_dicts(self.capabilities)
        self.metadata = _clean_dict(self.metadata)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "adapter_slug": self.adapter_slug,
            "platform": self.platform,
            "protocol_version": self.protocol_version,
            "status": self.status,
            "connected_at": self.connected_at,
            "capabilities": [dict(capability) for capability in self.capabilities],
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class AdapterExecutionRequest:
    action_type: str
    target: str
    payload: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    requested_at: str = field(default_factory=_utc_now)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.action_type = _require_text(self.action_type, "action_type")
        self.target = _require_text(self.target, "target")
        self.payload = _clean_dict(self.payload)
        self.requested_at = _require_text(self.requested_at, "requested_at")
        self.metadata = _clean_dict(self.metadata)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "action_type": self.action_type,
            "target": self.target,
            "payload": dict(self.payload),
            "requested_at": self.requested_at,
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class AdapterExecutionResult:
    adapter_slug: str
    platform: str
    success: bool
    status: AdapterExecutionStatus
    summary: str
    completed_at: str
    output: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.adapter_slug = _require_text(self.adapter_slug, "adapter_slug")
        self.platform = _require_text(self.platform, "platform")
        self.summary = _require_text(self.summary, "summary")
        self.completed_at = _require_text(self.completed_at, "completed_at")
        self.output = _clean_dict(self.output)
        self.metadata = _clean_dict(self.metadata)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "adapter_slug": self.adapter_slug,
            "platform": self.platform,
            "success": self.success,
            "status": self.status,
            "summary": self.summary,
            "completed_at": self.completed_at,
            "output": dict(self.output),
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


class SupportsAdapter(Protocol):
    record: IntegrationRecord

    def handshake(self) -> AdapterHandshake: ...
    def manifest(self) -> AdapterManifest: ...
    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult: ...


@dataclass(slots=True)
class BaseIntegrationAdapter:
    record: IntegrationRecord
    protocol_version: str = "1.0.0"
    health: AdapterHealth = "ready"
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.protocol_version = _require_text(self.protocol_version, "protocol_version")
        self.metadata = _clean_dict(self.metadata)

    @property
    def adapter_slug(self) -> str:
        return self.record.slug

    @property
    def platform(self) -> str:
        return self.record.platform

    def base_metadata(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "integration_id": self.record.integration_id,
            "integration_type": self.record.integration_type,
            "integration_status": self.record.status,
            "protocol_version": self.protocol_version,
            "adapter_health": self.health,
            **self.metadata,
        }

    def is_available(self) -> bool:
        return self.health != "offline"

    def supported_action_types(self) -> list[str]:
        return []

    def handshake(self) -> AdapterHandshake:
        return AdapterHandshake(
            adapter_slug=self.adapter_slug,
            platform=self.platform,
            protocol_version=self.protocol_version,
            status=self.health,
            connected_at=_utc_now(),
            capabilities=[capability.to_dict() for capability in self.record.capabilities],
            metadata=self.base_metadata(),
        )

    def manifest(self) -> AdapterManifest:
        return build_adapter_manifest(
            self.record,
            extra_metadata={
                **self.base_metadata(),
                "supported_action_types": self.supported_action_types(),
            },
        )

    def validate_request(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> None:
        supported = self.supported_action_types()
        if supported and request.action_type not in supported:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unsupported action_type '{request.action_type}' for adapter '{self.adapter_slug}'"
            )

    def build_result(
        self,
        *,
        request: AdapterExecutionRequest,
        success: bool,
        status: AdapterExecutionStatus,
        summary: str,
        output: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        result_output = {
            "request": request.to_dict(),
            "integration_id": self.record.integration_id,
            **_clean_dict(output),
        }
        result_metadata = {
            **self.base_metadata(),
            **_clean_dict(metadata),
        }
        return AdapterExecutionResult(
            adapter_slug=self.adapter_slug,
            platform=self.platform,
            success=success,
            status=status,
            summary=summary,
            completed_at=_utc_now(),
            output=result_output,
            metadata=result_metadata,
        )

    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        self.validate_request(request)

        if self.health == "offline":
            return self.build_result(
                request=request,
                success=False,
                status="offline",
                summary=f"{self.record.name} is offline and cannot execute '{request.action_type}'.",
            )

        status: AdapterExecutionStatus = (
            "accepted" if self.health == "ready" else "accepted_with_warnings"
        )
        summary = (
            f"{self.record.name} accepted action '{request.action_type}' for target '{request.target}'."
            if self.health == "ready"
            else f"{self.record.name} accepted action '{request.action_type}' for target '{request.target}' in degraded mode."
        )

        return self.build_result(
            request=request,
            success=True,
            status=status,
            summary=summary,
        )


def summarize_adapter_handshake(handshake: AdapterHandshake) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "adapter_slug": handshake.adapter_slug,
        "platform": handshake.platform,
        "protocol_version": handshake.protocol_version,
        "status": handshake.status,
        "capability_count": len(handshake.capabilities),
        "connected_at": handshake.connected_at,
    }


def summarize_adapter_execution(result: AdapterExecutionResult) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "adapter_slug": result.adapter_slug,
        "platform": result.platform,
        "success": result.success,
        "status": result.status,
        "completed_at": result.completed_at,
    }

def build_claude_code_adapter_request(
    *,
    action_type: str,
    target: str,
    content: str = "",
    client_id: str | None = None,
    session_id: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> ClaudeCodeAdapterRequest:
    normalized_action_type = _normalize_text(action_type)
    normalized_target = _normalize_text(target)

    if not normalized_action_type:
        raise ValueError("action_type is required")
    if not normalized_target:

        content=content or "",
        client_id=_normalize_text(client_id) or None,
        session_id=_normalize_text(session_id) or None,
        metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
    )


def adapt_policy_decision_to_claude_code(
    decision: PolicyDecision,
    *,
    mode: AdapterExecutionMode = "enforce",
    trace_id: str | None = None,
    request: ClaudeCodeAdapterRequest | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> ClaudeCodeAdapterResponse:
    verdict: AdapterVerdict = decision.verdict
    matched_rules = [match.rule_id for match in decision.matches]
    reasons = [match.to_dict() for match in decision.matches]

    return ClaudeCodeAdapterResponse(
        adapter_name="ironclaw-claude-code",
        platform="claude-code",
        mode=mode,
        verdict=verdict,
        should_allow=verdict == "allow",
        should_warn=verdict == "warn",
        should_quarantine=verdict == "quarantine",
        should_block=verdict == "block",
        risk_score=decision.risk_score,
        risk_level=decision.risk_level,
        summary=decision.summary,
        matched_rules=matched_rules,
        reasons=reasons,
        decision_id=decision.decision_id,
        trace_id=trace_id,
        request=request.to_dict() if request else {},
        metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
    )


def evaluate_claude_code_request(
    engine: PolicyEngine,
    request: ClaudeCodeAdapterRequest,
    *,
    risk_score: int = 0,
    mode: AdapterExecutionMode = "enforce",

) -> ClaudeCodeAdapterResponse:

    return adapt_policy_decision_to_claude_code(
        decision,

        request=request,
        metadata=metadata,
    )

@dataclass(slots=True)
class ClaudeCodeAdapter(BaseIntegrationAdapter):
    runtime: str = "claude-code"
    guard_mode: str = "strict"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.metadata.setdefault("runtime", self.runtime)
        self.metadata.setdefault("guard_mode", self.guard_mode)

    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        result = super().execute(request)
        result.status = "guarded"
        result.summary = f"{self.record.name} guarded action '{request.action_type}' for target '{request.target}'."
        result.output["guard_applied"] = True
        result.metadata["runtime"] = self.runtime
        result.metadata["guard_mode"] = self.guard_mode
        return result

# --- Integration adapter class + factory for tests ---


@dataclass(slots=True)
class GenericAgentAdapter(BaseIntegrationAdapter):
    """Integration adapter for 'integration-generic-agent' records."""

    runtime: str = "generic-agent"
    guard_mode: str = "strict"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # Ensure runtime and guard_mode are reflected in metadata for handshake/manifest.
        if "runtime" not in self.metadata:
            self.metadata["runtime"] = self.runtime
        if "guard_mode" not in self.metadata:
            self.metadata["guard_mode"] = self.guard_mode

    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        # Start from the base adapter execution result.
        result = super().execute(request)
        # Mark that IronClaw guard logic has been applied for this generic agent.
        result.status = "guarded"
        result.summary = (
            f"{self.record.name} guarded action "
            f"'{request.action_type}' for target '{request.target}'."
        )
        result.output.setdefault("request", request.to_dict())
        result.output["guard_applied"] = True
        result.metadata["runtime"] = self.runtime
        result.metadata["guard_mode"] = self.guard_mode
        return result


def build_generic_agent_adapter(registry: IntegrationRegistry) -> GenericAgentAdapter:
    """Factory for the generic-agent adapter used in tests and integrations."""
    record: IntegrationRecord | None = get_integration(registry, "integration-generic-agent")
    if record is None:
        raise KeyError("unknown integration_id: integration-generic-agent")

    return GenericAgentAdapter(
        record=record,
        protocol_version="1.0.0",
        health="ready",
        metadata={
            "runtime": "generic-agent",
            "guard_mode": "strict",
        },
    )

McpToolCallPhase = Literal["plan", "preflight", "execute"]
McpToolKind = Literal["mcp", "openai-tool", "custom"]
McpGuardMode = Literal["monitor", "enforce"]


def _utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _normalize_text(value: str | None) -> str:
    return (value or "").strip()


def _clean_dict(value: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return dict(value or {})


def _clean_list(value: list[Any] | None) -> list[Any]:
    return list(value or [])


@dataclass(slots=True)
class McpToolInvocation:
    """High-level description of a tool invocation coming from an MCP/tool client."""

    tool_name: str
    phase: McpToolCallPhase
    arguments: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    client_id: str | None = None
    session_id: str | None = None
    agent_id: str | None = None
    agent_name: str | None = None
    runtime_name: str | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.tool_name = _normalize_text(self.tool_name)
        self.phase = _normalize_text(self.phase) or "execute"  # type: ignore[assignment]
        self.arguments = _clean_dict(self.arguments)
        self.client_id = _normalize_text(self.client_id) or None
        self.session_id = _normalize_text(self.session_id) or None
        self.agent_id = _normalize_text(self.agent_id) or None
        self.agent_name = _normalize_text(self.agent_name) or None
        self.runtime_name = _normalize_text(self.runtime_name) or None
        self.metadata = _clean_dict(self.metadata)

    def to_adapter_request(self) -> AdapterExecutionRequest:
        """Adapt to the generic AdapterExecutionRequest envelope."""
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "tool_name": self.tool_name,
            "phase": self.phase,
            "arguments": dict(self.arguments),
            "client_id": self.client_id,
            "session_id": self.session_id,
            "agent_id": self.agent_id,
            "agent_name": self.agent_name,
            "runtime_name": self.runtime_name,
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }
        payload = {k: v for k, v in payload.items() if v is not None}

        return AdapterExecutionRequest(
            action_type=f"toolcall:{self.phase}",
            target=f"tool://{self.tool_name}",
            payload=payload,
            metadata={},
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "tool_name": self.tool_name,
            "phase": self.phase,
            "arguments": dict(self.arguments),
            "client_id": self.client_id,
            "session_id": self.session_id,
            "agent_id": self.agent_id,
            "agent_name": self.agent_name,
            "runtime_name": self.runtime_name,
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class McpToolGuardDecision:
    """Result of guarding a tool invocation before or after real execution."""

    adapter_name: str

    status: AdapterExecutionStatus
    should_allow: bool
    should_warn: bool

    matched_rules: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    decision_id: str | None = None

    decided_at: str = field(default_factory=_utc_now)
    request: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {

            "platform": self.platform,
            "mode": self.mode,
            "verdict": self.verdict,
            "status": self.status,
            "should_allow": self.should_allow,
            "should_warn": self.should_warn,
            "should_block": self.should_block,
            "should_review": self.should_review,
            "summary": self.summary,
            "risk_score": self.risk_score,
            "risk_level": self.risk_level,
            "matched_rules": _clean_list(self.matched_rules),
            "reasons": _clean_list(self.reasons),
            "decision_id": self.decision_id,
            "trace_id": self.trace_id,
            "decided_at": self.decided_at,
            "request": dict(self.request),

@dataclass(slots=True)
class McpToolAdapter(BaseIntegrationAdapter):
    """Integration adapter that wraps MCP/server tools behind the base adapter contract."""

    kind: McpToolKind = "mcp"
    guard_mode: McpGuardMode = "enforce"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if "kind" not in self.metadata:
            self.metadata["kind"] = self.kind
        if "guard_mode" not in self.metadata:
            self.metadata["guard_mode"] = self.guard_mode

    def supported_action_types(self) -> list[str]:
        # All toolcall phases go through this adapter.
        return [
            "toolcall:plan",
            "toolcall:preflight",
            "toolcall:execute",
        ]

    def _tool_capabilities(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        caps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for capability in self.record.capabilities:
            if isinstance(capability, IntegrationCapability):
                caps.append(capability.to_dict())
            else:
                caps.append(getattr(capability, "to_dict", lambda: dict(capability))())
        return caps

    def guard_invocation(
        self,
        invocation: McpToolInvocation,
        *,
        mode: McpGuardMode = "enforce",
        trace_id: str | None = None,
        risk_score: int = 0,
        risk_level: str = "low",
        matched_rules: list[str] | None = None,
        reasons: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    ) -> McpToolGuardDecision:
        """Placeholder hook where policy / Groq verdict logic will plug in."""
        should_review = mode == "enforce" and invocation.phase != "plan"
        verdict = "allow"
        status: AdapterExecutionStatus = "guarded"

        summary = (
            f"Guarded tool '{invocation.tool_name}' at phase '{invocation.phase}' "
            f"for runtime '{invocation.runtime_name or 'unknown-runtime'}'."
        )

        return McpToolGuardDecision(
            adapter_name=self.record.name,
            platform=self.record.platform,
            mode=mode,
            verdict=verdict,
            status=status,
            should_allow=True,
            should_warn=False,
            should_block=False,
            should_review=should_review,
            summary=summary,
            risk_score=risk_score,
            risk_level=risk_level,
            matched_rules=_clean_list(matched_rules),
            reasons=_clean_list(reasons),
            decision_id=None,
            trace_id=trace_id,
            request=invocation.to_dict(),
            metadata={
                **self.base_metadata(),
                "tool_name": invocation.tool_name,
                "phase": invocation.phase,
            },
        )

    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        """
        Execute a tool call through the base adapter contract.

        At this layer we do not talk to a real MCP server yet; we envelope the request,
        attach guard decision metadata, and let upstream orchestration decide how to
        route the actual tool execution for IronClaw-Security.
        """
        # Let the base adapter validate action_type/target and health first.
        base_result = super().execute(request)

        # Derive tool name + phase from the request envelope if present.
        tool_name = _normalize_text(request.payload.get("tool_name")) or request.target
        phase = _normalize_text(request.payload.get("phase")) or "execute"

        invocation = McpToolInvocation(
            tool_name=tool_name,
            phase=phase,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            arguments=request.payload.get("arguments") or {},
            client_id=request.payload.get("client_id"),
            session_id=request.payload.get("session_id"),
            agent_id=request.payload.get("agent_id"),
            agent_name=request.payload.get("agent_name"),
            runtime_name=request.payload.get("runtime_name"),
            metadata=request.payload.get("metadata") or {},
        )

        decision = self.guard_invocation(invocation, mode=self.guard_mode)

        # Attach guard decision into the adapter result without changing success.
        base_result.status = decision.status
        base_result.summary = decision.summary
        base_result.output.setdefault("request", request.to_dict())
        base_result.output["guard_decision"] = decision.to_dict()
        base_result.metadata["guard_mode"] = self.guard_mode
        base_result.metadata["kind"] = self.kind

        return base_result


def build_mcp_tool_adapter(registry: IntegrationRegistry) -> McpToolAdapter:
    """
    Factory for the MCP tool adapter used in tests and integrations.

    Expects an IntegrationRecord with id 'integration-mcp-tools' to exist in the registry.
    """
    record: IntegrationRecord | None = get_integration(
        registry,
        "integration-mcp-tools",
    )
    if record is None:
        raise KeyError("unknown integration_id: integration-mcp-tools")

    return McpToolAdapter(
        record=record,
        protocol_version="1.0.0",
        health="ready",
        metadata={
            "kind": "mcp",
            "guard_mode": "enforce",
        },
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Literal

from app.adapters.base import (
    AdapterExecutionRequest,
    AdapterExecutionResult,
    BaseIntegrationAdapter,
)
from app.orchestrator.policy_enforcer import (
    PolicyDecision,
    PolicyEngine,
    PolicyInput,
    evaluate_policy,
)
from app.services.integration_registry import (
    IntegrationRegistry,
    get_integration,
)

AdapterVerdict = Literal["allow", "warn", "quarantine", "block"]
AdapterExecutionMode = Literal["monitor", "enforce"]


def _utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _normalize_text(value: str | None) -> str:
    return (value or "").strip()


# ---------- Policy-facing adapter request/response ----------


@dataclass(slots=True)
class OpenClawAdapterRequest:
    """
    High-level request wrapper for OpenClaw builder/workflow actions.

    This is the policy-facing representation of an OpenClaw action that will be
    evaluated by the IronClaw policy engine.
    """

    action_type: str
    target: str
    content: str = ""
    builder_id: str | None = None
    workflow_id: str | None = None
    client_id: str | None = None
    session_id: str | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_policy_input(self) -> PolicyInput:
        """
        Convert this request into a PolicyInput for the policy engine.

        builder_id and workflow_id are folded into metadata so they can be
        targeted by policy rules without changing the PolicyInput shape.
        """
        merged_metadata: dict[str, Any] = dict(self.metadata)
        if self.builder_id:
            merged_metadata["builder_id"] = self.builder_id
        if self.workflow_id:
            merged_metadata["workflow_id"] = self.workflow_id

        return PolicyInput(
            action_type=self.action_type,
            target=self.target,
            content=self.content,
            client_id=self.client_id,
            session_id=self.session_id,
            metadata=merged_metadata,
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Serialize this request into a JSON-safe dict for logging/telemetry.
        """
        return {
            "action_type": self.action_type,
            "target": self.target,
            "content": self.content,
            "builder_id": self.builder_id,
            "workflow_id": self.workflow_id,
            "client_id": self.client_id,
            "session_id": self.session_id,
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class OpenClawAdapterResponse:
    """
    Normalized policy decision payload for OpenClaw.

    This wraps a PolicyDecision with OpenClaw-specific flags (should_hold, etc.)
    so the builder/workflow runtime can make simple allow/hold decisions.
    """

    adapter_name: str
    platform: str
    mode: AdapterExecutionMode
    verdict: AdapterVerdict
    should_allow: bool
    should_warn: bool
    should_quarantine: bool
    should_block: bool
    should_hold: bool
    risk_score: int
    risk_level: str
    summary: str
    matched_rules: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    reasons: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    decision_id: str | None = None
    trace_id: str | None = None
    reviewed_at: str = field(default_factory=_utc_now)
    request: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Serialize this response into a JSON-safe dict for logging/telemetry.
        """
        return {
            "adapter_name": self.adapter_name,
            "platform": self.platform,
            "mode": self.mode,
            "verdict": self.verdict,
            "should_allow": self.should_allow,
            "should_warn": self.should_warn,
            "should_quarantine": self.should_quarantine,
            "should_block": self.should_block,
            "should_hold": self.should_hold,
            "risk_score": self.risk_score,
            "risk_level": self.risk_level,
            "summary": self.summary,
            "matched_rules": list(self.matched_rules),
            "reasons": list(self.reasons),
            "decision_id": self.decision_id,
            "trace_id": self.trace_id,
            "reviewed_at": self.reviewed_at,
            "request": dict(self.request),
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


def build_openclaw_adapter_request(
    *,
    action_type: str,
    target: str,
    content: str = "",
    builder_id: str | None = None,
    workflow_id: str | None = None,
    client_id: str | None = None,
    session_id: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> OpenClawAdapterRequest:
    """
    Convenience constructor that normalizes and validates inbound fields.

    Ensures action_type and target are non-empty, trims string fields, and
    shields callers from having to know about default metadata behavior.
    """
    normalized_action_type = _normalize_text(action_type)
    normalized_target = _normalize_text(target)

    if not normalized_action_type:
        raise ValueError("action_type is required")
    if not normalized_target:
        raise ValueError("target is required")

    return OpenClawAdapterRequest(
        action_type=normalized_action_type,
        target=normalized_target,
        content=content or "",
        builder_id=_normalize_text(builder_id) or None,
        workflow_id=_normalize_text(workflow_id) or None,
        client_id=_normalize_text(client_id) or None,
        session_id=_normalize_text(session_id) or None,
        metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
    )


def adapt_policy_decision_to_openclaw(
    decision: PolicyDecision,
    *,
    mode: AdapterExecutionMode = "enforce",
    trace_id: str | None = None,
    request: OpenClawAdapterRequest | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> OpenClawAdapterResponse:
    """
    Map a PolicyDecision into an OpenClawAdapterResponse.

    should_hold is when a decision is anything other than allow so the
    OpenClaw runtime can pause the workflow until a human reviews.
    """
    verdict: AdapterVerdict = decision.verdict
    matched_rules = [match.rule_id for match in decision.matches]
    reasons = [match.to_dict() for match in decision.matches]
    should_hold = verdict in {"warn", "quarantine", "block"}

    return OpenClawAdapterResponse(
        adapter_name="ironclaw-openclaw",
        platform="openclaw",
        mode=mode,
        verdict=verdict,
        should_allow=verdict == "allow",
        should_warn=verdict == "warn",
        should_quarantine=verdict == "quarantine",
        should_block=verdict == "block",
        should_hold=should_hold,
        risk_score=decision.risk_score,
        risk_level=decision.risk_level,
        summary=decision.summary,
        matched_rules=matched_rules,
        reasons=reasons,
        decision_id=decision.decision_id,
        trace_id=trace_id,
        request=request.to_dict() if request else {},
        metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
    )


def evaluate_openclaw_request(
    engine: PolicyEngine,
    request: OpenClawAdapterRequest,
    *,
    risk_score: int = 0,
    mode: AdapterExecutionMode = "enforce",
    trace_id: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> OpenClawAdapterResponse:
    """
    One-shot helper: evaluate a request and return an OpenClawAdapterResponse.
    """
    decision = evaluate_policy(
        engine,
        request.to_policy_input(),
        risk_score=risk_score,
    )
    return adapt_policy_decision_to_openclaw(
        decision,
        mode=mode,
        trace_id=trace_id,
        request=request,
        metadata=metadata,
    )


def summarize_openclaw_adapter_response(
    response: OpenClawAdapterResponse,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Compact summary record for dashboards, logs, or telemetry streams.
    """
    return {
        "adapter_name": response.adapter_name,
        "platform": response.platform,
        "mode": response.mode,
        "verdict": response.verdict,
        "should_hold": response.should_hold,
        "risk_score": response.risk_score,
        "risk_level": response.risk_level,
        "summary": response.summary,
        "matched_rule_count": len(response.matched_rules),
        "decision_id": response.decision_id,
        "trace_id": response.trace_id,
        "reviewed_at": response.reviewed_at,
    }


# ---------- Integration-facing OpenClaw adapter class ----------


@dataclass(slots=True)
class OpenClawAdapter(BaseIntegrationAdapter):
    """
    Integration adapter for the OpenClaw runtime.

    This wraps guarded OpenClaw workflow executions and annotates results so the
    IronClaw UI can show that a builder workflow was gate-kept by policy.
    """

    runtime: str = "openclaw"
    workflow_mode: str = "builder-guard"
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # Ensure core metadata keys are present and stable for handshakes/manifests.
        self.metadata.setdefault("integration_id", self.record.integration_id)
        self.metadata.setdefault("runtime", self.runtime)
        self.metadata.setdefault("workflow_mode", self.workflow_mode)

    def execute(self, request: AdapterExecutionRequest) -> AdapterExecutionResult:
        """
        Execute a guarded OpenClaw workflow action.

        For now we delegate to the BaseIntegrationAdapter for any shared plumbing
        and then mark the result as "guarded" with OpenClaw-specific metadata.
        """
        result = super().execute(request)

        # Mark this as a guarded workflow execution for dashboards/telemetry.
        result.status = "guarded"
        result.summary = (
            f"{self.record.name} guarded workflow action "
            f"'{request.action_type}' for target '{request.target}'."
        )

        # Attach guard-specific output details and a minimal echo of the request.
        result.output.setdefault("guard_applied", True)
        result.output.setdefault("execution_mode", "workflow-gated")
        result.output.setdefault(
            "request",
            {
                "action_type": request.action_type,
                "target": request.target,
                "payload": request.payload,
            },
        )

        # Propagate runtime metadata so tests and UI can assert on it.
        result.metadata.setdefault("runtime", self.runtime)
        result.metadata.setdefault("workflow_mode", self.workflow_mode)

        return result


def build_openclaw_adapter(registry: IntegrationRegistry) -> OpenClawAdapter:
    """
    Factory to construct an OpenClawAdapter from the integration registry.

    Expected to back tests in tests/test_openclaw_adapter.py.
    """
    record = get_integration(registry, "integration-openclaw")
    if record is None:
        raise KeyError("unknown integration_id: integration-openclaw")

    return OpenClawAdapter(
        record=record,
        protocol_version="1.0.0",
        health="ready",
        metadata={
            "integration_id": record.integration_id,
            "runtime": "openclaw",
            "workflow_mode": "builder-guard",
        },
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Mapping, Sequence

from app.runtime.sandboxrouter import (
    SandboxExecutionRequest,
    SandboxExecutionResult,
    build_sandbox_router,
)


ExecutorCallable = Callable[..., Any]


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SandboxRuntimeAdapter:
    router: Any = field(default_factory=build_sandbox_router)
    executor: ExecutorCallable | None = None
    name: str = "sandboxruntimeadapter"

    def execute(
        self,
        *,
        actiontype: str,
        target: str,
        command: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        network_url: str | None = None,
        network_method: str = "GET",
        artifact_paths: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        content: str | bytes | None = None,
        cwd: str | None = None,
        timeout_seconds: int = 30,
        environment_scope: str = "sandbox",
        metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        request = SandboxExecutionRequest(
            actiontype=actiontype,
            target=target,
            command=command,
            network_url=network_url,
            network_method=network_method,
            artifact_paths=[str(item) for item in (artifact_paths or []) if str(item).strip()],
            content=content,
            cwd=cwd,
            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
            environment_scope=environment_scope,
            metadata={
                **dict(metadata or {}),
                "adapter": self.name,
            },
        )

        result = self.router.route(
            request=request,
            executor=self.executor,
        )
        return self._normalize_result(result=result)

    def evaluate_only(
        self,
        *,
        actiontype: str,
        target: str,
        command: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        network_url: str | None = None,
        network_method: str = "GET",
        artifact_paths: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        content: str | bytes | None = None,
        cwd: str | None = None,
        timeout_seconds: int = 30,
        environment_scope: str = "sandbox",
        metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        request = SandboxExecutionRequest(
            actiontype=actiontype,
            target=target,
            command=command,
            network_url=network_url,
            network_method=network_method,
            artifact_paths=[str(item) for item in (artifact_paths or []) if str(item).strip()],
            content=content,
            cwd=cwd,
            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
            environment_scope=environment_scope,
            metadata={
                **dict(metadata or {}),
                "adapter": self.name,
                "mode": "evaluate_only",
            },
        )

        decision = self.router.evaluate(request=request)
        return decision.as_dict()

    def _normalize_result(self, *, result: SandboxExecutionResult) -> dict[str, Any]:
        payload = result.as_dict()
        payload.setdefault("adapter", self.name)
        payload.setdefault("runtime", "sandbox")
        return payload


def initialize_sandboxruntimeadapter(
    *,
    router: Any | None = None,
    executor: ExecutorCallable | None = None,
) -> SandboxRuntimeAdapter:
    return SandboxRuntimeAdapter(
        router=router or build_sandbox_router(),
        executor=executor,
    )


def build_sandboxruntimeadapter() -> SandboxRuntimeAdapter:
    return initialize_sandboxruntimeadapter()

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Header

from app.dependencies.auth import require_authenticated
from app.dependencies.org_context import get_org_context
from app.dependencies.operator_auth import (
    require_operator_auth,
    require_operator_manage,
    require_operator_permission,
    require_operator_read,
)
from app.dependencies.permissions import (
    require_all_permissions,
    require_any_permission,
    require_permissions_read,
    require_permissions_write,
)


router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/access-control", tags=["access-control"])


@router.get("/context")
async def get_access_control_context_endpoint(
    context=Depends(require_authenticated),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "authenticated": True,
        "principal_id": context.principal_id,
        "principal_type": context.principal_type,
        "org_id": context.org_id,
        "roles": list(context.roles),
        "permissions": list(context.permissions),
        "session_id": context.session_id,

from __future__ import annotations

from http import HTTPStatus
from typing import Any, Literal, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.guard.facade import guardandexecuteaction
from app.orchestrator.secureruntimepipeline import SecureRuntimePipeline, getactionexecutepipeline

router = APIRouter()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pydantic models
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ExecuteRequest(BaseModel):
    """
    Incoming request for guarded action execution.
    Mirrors the payload used in testsactionexecute.py.
    """

    actiontype: str = Field(..., description="High-level action type, e.g. httpfetch or toolcall.")
    target: str = Field(..., description="Execution target, e.g. URL or tool identifier.")
    content: str = Field(..., description="Human-readable description or prompt text.")
    riskscore: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100, description="Pre-computed risk score 0-100.")
    clientid: str = Field(..., description="Logical client identifier.")
    sessionid: str = Field(..., description="Execution/session correlation id.")
    filepath: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Logical source filepath for this action; defaults to app/api/action/execute.py.",
    )


ExecutionStatus = Literal["completed", "queuedforreview", "denied"]
ResponseAction = Literal["allow", "warn", "quarantine", "block", "review"]
PolicyVerdict = Literal["allow", "warn", "quarantine", "block"]


class ExecuteResponse(BaseModel):
    """
    HTTP facade response for guarded execution.
    Constrained to the literals expected by tests and downâ€‘stream callers.
    """

    # Core execution state
    executionstate: ExecutionStatus = Field(
        ...,
        description="High-level execution outcome: completed, queuedforreview, or denied.",
    )
    responseaction: ResponseAction = Field(
        ...,
        description="Action recommended/applied by policy and boundary.",
    )
    responsestatus: ExecutionStatus = Field(
        ...,
        description="HTTP-style status mapped into the same execution status domain.",
    )

    # Decision / policy metadata
    policyverdict: PolicyVerdict = Field(
        ...,
        description="Final policy verdict: allow, warn, quarantine, or block.",
    )
    riskscore: int = Field(
        ...,
        ge=0,
        le=100,
        description="Echoed risk score, for client-side introspection.",
    )
    shouldexecute: bool = Field(
        ...,
        description="Whether the action should actually execute beyond dry-run.",
    )
    haltedbyboundary: bool = Field(
        ...,
        description="True if boundary logic prevented real execution.",
    )
    reviewitemid: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Identifier of a queued review item when queuedforreview.",
    )

    # Tracing / correlation
    executionid: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Opaque identifier for this guarded execution.",
    )
    traceid: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Distributed trace correlation id (if available).",
    )
    requestid: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Logical request id, may map to gateway / ingress id.",
    )
    decisionid: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Identifier for the policy decision entry.",
    )

    # Executor details
    executorname: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Name of the executor used: dryrunexecutor, real executor, etc.",
    )
    executorresult: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Opaque executor result payload, if available.",
    )

    # Human-readable explanation
    reason: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        description="Primary human-readable reason string for the decision.",
    )
    reasons: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Structured list of contributing reasons with scores/labels.",
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


_DEFAULT_FILEPATH = "app/api/action/execute.py"


def _map_http_status_to_execution_status(status_code: int) -> ExecutionStatus:
    """
    Map numeric HTTP-ish status into the literal status domain required
    by ExecuteResponse.responsestatus and .executionstate.

    Tests assert that only 'completed', 'queuedforreview', or 'denied'
    are ever present here.[file:4]
    """
    if status_code in (HTTPStatus.OK, HTTPStatus.CREATED, HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED):
        return "completed"
    if status_code in (
        HTTPStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
        HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
        HTTPStatus.LOCKED,
    ):
        return "queuedforreview"
    # 4xx/5xx and anything unexpected collapse to denied
    return "denied"


def _normalize_policy_verdict(raw: Optional[str]) -> PolicyVerdict:
    """
    Ensure policyverdict stays within the allowed literal set.
    Some older components may emit 'deny'; tests expect block/quarantine
    membership checks instead.[file:4]
    """
    if not raw:
        return "allow"

    value = raw.lower()
    if value in {"allow", "warn", "quarantine", "block"}:
        return value  # type: ignore[return-value]

    # Backwards-compat: unify any deny/forbid style to 'block'
    return "block"


def _normalize_response_action(raw: Optional[str], verdict: PolicyVerdict) -> ResponseAction:
    """
    Normalize the raw response action from lower layers to the allowed literals.
    Tests assert responseaction is in allow, warn, quarantine, block, review.[file:4]
    """
    if not raw:
        # Derive from verdict when missing.
        if verdict in ("allow", "warn"):
            return verdict
        if verdict in ("quarantine", "block"):
            return verdict
        return "review"

    value = raw.lower()
    if value in {"allow", "warn", "quarantine", "block", "review"}:
        return value  # type: ignore[return-value]

    if value in {"deny", "denied"}:
        return "block"

    # Fallback to verdict alignment.
    if verdict in ("allow", "warn"):
        return verdict
    if verdict in ("quarantine", "block"):
        return verdict
    return "review"


def _normalize_execution_state(raw_state: Optional[str], status: ExecutionStatus) -> ExecutionStatus:
    """
    Normalize executionstate to the literal domain required by the tests,
    using either the raw state emitted by summarizeexecution or the
    mapped HTTPish status code.[file:1]
    """
    if raw_state:
        value = raw_state.lower()
        if value in {"completed", "executed", "succeeded", "ok"}:
            return "completed"
        if value in {"queuedforreview", "queued", "pending_review", "pending"}:
            return "queuedforreview"
        if value in {"denied", "blocked", "failed", "error"}:
            return "denied"

    # Fall back to the mapped status when the raw state is unknown/missing.
    return status


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Route
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@router.post(
    "/execute",
    response_model=ExecuteResponse,
    summary="Guard and execute an action through the secure runtime pipeline.",
)
def guardedexecute(
    payload: ExecuteRequest,
    pipeline: SecureRuntimePipeline = Depends(getactionexecutepipeline),
) -> ExecuteResponse:
    """
    Guard and optionally execute an action.

    This is the HTTP facade used by testsactionexecute.py as `client.post('/guard/execute')`
    (or similar alias), and it delegates to the guardandexecuteaction facade which in turn
    calls executeguardedaction and the SecureRuntimePipeline.[file:1]
    """
    effective_filepath = payload.filepath or _DEFAULT_FILEPATH

    # Delegate to facade; this returns an ActionExecuteResult instance.
    responsepayload = guardandexecuteaction(
        actiontype=payload.actiontype,
        target=payload.target,
        content=payload.content,
        riskscore=payload.riskscore,
        clientid=payload.clientid,
        sessionid=payload.sessionid,
        filepath=effective_filepath,
        pipeline=pipeline,
    )

    # Extract raw fields from ActionExecuteResult / summary dict.
    # We access via getattr to tolerate both object-style and dict-style results.[file:1]
    def _get(field: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
        if isinstance(responsepayload, dict):
            return responsepayload.get(field, default)
        return getattr(responsepayload, field, default)

    raw_status_code: int = int(_get("responsestatus", HTTPStatus.OK))
    mapped_status: ExecutionStatus = _map_http_status_to_execution_status(raw_status_code)

    raw_exec_state: Optional[str] = _get("executionstate")
    execution_state: ExecutionStatus = _normalize_execution_state(raw_exec_state, mapped_status)

    raw_policy_verdict: Optional[str] = _get("policyverdict")
    policy_verdict: PolicyVerdict = _normalize_policy_verdict(raw_policy_verdict)

    raw_response_action: Optional[str] = _get("responseaction")
    response_action: ResponseAction = _normalize_response_action(raw_response_action, policy_verdict)

    # Build the response with safe fallbacks where older components might omit fields.
    return ExecuteResponse(
        executionstate=execution_state,
        responseaction=response_action,
        responsestatus=mapped_status,
        policyverdict=policy_verdict,
        riskscore=int(_get("riskscore", payload.riskscore)),
        shouldexecute=bool(_get("shouldexecute", False)),
        haltedbyboundary=bool(_get("haltedbyboundary", False)),
        reviewitemid=_get("reviewitemid"),
        executionid=_get("executionid"),
        traceid=_get("traceid"),
        requestid=_get("requestid"),
        decisionid=_get("decisionid"),
        executorname=_get("executorname"),
        executorresult=_get("executorresult"),
        reason=_get("reason"),
        reasons=list(_get("reasons", [])) or [],
    )

from __future__ import annotations


from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request


from app.dependencies.action_execute import get_action_execute_pipeline
from app.facade import guardandexecuteaction
from app.models.action_execute import ExecuteRequest, ExecuteResponse
from app.orchestrator.secure_runtime_pipeline import SecureRuntimePipeline
from app.services.telemetry import append_telemetry_event


router = APIRouter()



def _request_meta(request: Request) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    return {
        "request_id": getattr(request.state, "request_id", None),
        "trace_id": getattr(request.state, "trace_id", None),
        "path": request.url.path,
        "method": request.method,
    }



@router.post("/execute", response_model=ExecuteResponse)
def guarded_execute(
    payload: ExecuteRequest,
    request: Request,
    pipeline: SecureRuntimePipeline = Depends(get_action_execute_pipeline),
) -> ExecuteResponse:
    try:
        append_telemetry_event(
            "guard_execute_requested",
            {
                **_request_meta(request),
                "action_type": payload.action_type,
                "target": payload.target,
                "client_id": payload.client_id,
                "session_id": payload.session_id,
            },
        )
    except Exception:
        pass

    response_payload = guardandexecuteaction(
        payload,
        pipeline=pipeline,
    )

    response = ExecuteResponse(**response_payload)

    try:
        append_telemetry_event(
            "guard_execute_completed",
            {
                **_request_meta(request),
                "action_type": payload.action_type,
                "target": payload.target,
                "client_id": payload.client_id,
                "session_id": payload.session_id,
                "execution_id": getattr(response, "execution_id", None),
                "execution_state": getattr(response, "execution_state", None),
                "response_action": getattr(response, "response_action", None),
                "response_status": getattr(response, "response_status", None),
                "trace_id_response": getattr(response, "trace_id", None),
                "request_id_response": getattr(response, "request_id", None),
            },
        )
    except Exception:
        pass

    return response

from __future__ import annotations


from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request

)

_ALLOWED_REASON_SOURCES = {"policy", "scan", "ai"}
_REASON_SOURCE_MAP = {
    "promptinjection": "scan",
    "prompt_injection": "scan",
}


def _normalize_reason_source(source: object) -> str:
    value = str(source or "scan").strip().lower()
    if value in _ALLOWED_REASON_SOURCES:
        return value
    return _REASON_SOURCE_MAP.get(value, "scan")


def _normalize_reasons(reasons: list[object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    normalized: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    for item in reasons:
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            normalized.append(
                {
                    "source": _normalize_reason_source(item.get("source")),
                    "label": str(item.get("label") or item.get("code") or "Explanation"),
                    "details": str(
                        item.get("details")
                        or item.get("message")
                        or item.get("summary")
                        or ""
                    ),
                    "score": (
                        float(item["score"])
                        if item.get("score") is not None
                        else None
                    ),
                }
            )
        else:
            normalized.append(
                {
                    "source": "scan",
                    "label": "Explanation",
                    "details": str(item),
                    "score": None,
                }
            )

    return normalized


def _request_context(payload: ActionGuardRequest, request: Request) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "action_type": payload.action_type,
        "target": payload.target,
        "client_id": payload.client_id,
        "session_id": payload.session_id,
        "request_id": getattr(request.state, "request_id", None),
        "trace_id": getattr(request.state, "trace_id", None),
        "path": request.url.path,
        "method": request.method,
    }


@router.post("/action", response_model=ActionGuardResponse)
def guard_action(payload: ActionGuardRequest, request: Request) -> ActionGuardResponse:
    append_telemetry_event(
        "guard_action_requested",
        _request_context(payload, request),
    )

    result: ActionGuardDecision = analyze_action(
        action_type=payload.action_type,
        target=payload.target,
        content=payload.content,
        client_id=payload.client_id,
        session_id=payload.session_id,
    )
    result["reasons"] = _normalize_reasons(result.get("reasons", []))

    response = ActionGuardResponse(**result)

    append_telemetry_event(
        "guard_action_completed",
        {
            **_request_context(payload, request),
            "risk_score": getattr(response, "risk_score", None),
            "verdict": getattr(response, "verdict", None),
            "reason_count": len(getattr(response, "reasons", [])),
        },
    )

    return response

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.api.actionguard import guardaction


router = APIRouter(prefix="/decision", tags=["action-decision"])


DecisionOutcome = Literal["allow", "review", "quarantine", "deny"]
DecisionState = Literal["approved", "queuedforreview", "quarantined", "denied"]


class ActionDecisionRequest(BaseModel):
    actiontype: str = Field(..., description="Action type such as httpfetch or toolcall.")
    target: str = Field(..., description="Target such as URL, shell, file path, or tool id.")
    content: str = Field(..., description="Prompt or action content to evaluate.")
    riskscore: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100, description="Base risk score before decision logic.")
    clientid: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Client or actor id.")
    sessionid: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Session or workflow id.")
    filepath: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Optional source filepath for attribution.")
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Optional metadata from retrieved docs, tools, files, or model outputs.",
    )


class DecisionReasonView(BaseModel):
    source: str
    label: str
    details: str
    score: int


class ActionDecisionResponse(BaseModel):
    actiontype: str
    target: str
    outcome: DecisionOutcome
    state: DecisionState
    shouldexecute: bool
    haltedbyboundary: bool
    requiresreview: bool
    filepath: str
    baseriskscore: int
    adjustedriskscore: int
    reason: str
    reasons: list[DecisionReasonView] = Field(default_factory=list)
    promptinjection: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)


def decideaction(
    *,
    actiontype: str,
    target: str,
    content: str,
    riskscore: int,
    clientid: str | None = None,
    sessionid: str | None = None,
    filepath: str | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    guard = guardaction(
        actiontype=actiontype,
        target=target,
        content=content,
        riskscore=riskscore,
        clientid=clientid,
        sessionid=sessionid,
        filepath=filepath,
        metadata=metadata,
    )

    verdict = guard["verdict"]
    if verdict == "allow":
        outcome: DecisionOutcome = "allow"
        state: DecisionState = "approved"
        shouldexecute = True
        haltedbyboundary = False
        requiresreview = False
        reason = "Decision engine approved execution."
    elif verdict == "review":
        outcome = "review"
        state = "queuedforreview"
        shouldexecute = True
        haltedbyboundary = False
        requiresreview = True
        reason = "Decision engine queued the action for review."
    elif verdict == "quarantine":
        outcome = "quarantine"
        state = "quarantined"
        shouldexecute = False
        haltedbyboundary = True
        requiresreview = False
        reason = "Decision engine quarantined execution."
    else:
        outcome = "deny"
        state = "denied"
        shouldexecute = False
        haltedbyboundary = True
        requiresreview = False
        reason = "Decision engine denied execution."

    return {
        "actiontype": actiontype,
        "target": target,
        "outcome": outcome,
        "state": state,
        "shouldexecute": shouldexecute,
        "haltedbyboundary": haltedbyboundary,
        "requiresreview": requiresreview,
        "filepath": guard["filepath"],
        "baseriskscore": guard["baseriskscore"],
        "adjustedriskscore": guard["adjustedriskscore"],
        "reason": reason,
        "reasons": guard["reasons"],
        "promptinjection": guard["promptinjection"],
    }


@router.post(
    "/action",
    response_model=ActionDecisionResponse,
    summary="Produce the final runtime action decision with prompt injection awareness.",
)
def actiondecision(payload: ActionDecisionRequest) -> ActionDecisionResponse:
    result = decideaction(
        actiontype=payload.actiontype,
        target=payload.target,
        content=payload.content,
        riskscore=payload.riskscore,
        clientid=payload.clientid,
        sessionid=payload.sessionid,
        filepath=payload.filepath,
        metadata=payload.metadata,
    )
    return ActionDecisionResponse(**result)

    )


class ActionExecuteResponse(BaseModel):
    status: Literal["allowed", "review", "quarantined", "denied"]
    actiontype: str
    target: str
    ownerkey: str
    requestedunits: int
    finalriskscore: int
    promptinjection: dict[str, Any]
    audit: dict[str, Any]
    executionallowed: bool
    usage: dict[str, Any]
    message: str


def _map_audit_event_to_status(
    eventtype: str,
) -> Literal["allowed", "review", "quarantined", "denied"]:
    if eventtype == "execution_allowed":
        return "allowed"
    if eventtype == "execution_review":
        return "review"
    if eventtype == "execution_quarantined":
        return "quarantined"
    return "denied"


def _empty_usage(reason: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "executionid": None,
        "executed": False,
        "consumedunits": 0,
        "remainingunits": 0,
        "reason": reason,
        "applied": False,
        "plan": None,
        "subscriptionid": None,
        "walletbalance": None,
    }


def _usage_to_dict(receipt: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    consumption = getattr(receipt, "consumption", None)
    return {
        "executionid": getattr(receipt, "execution_id", None),
        "executed": getattr(receipt, "executed", False),
        "consumedunits": getattr(receipt, "consumed_units", 0),
        "remainingunits": getattr(receipt, "remaining_units", 0),
        "reason": getattr(receipt, "reason", ""),
        "applied": bool(getattr(consumption, "applied", False)) if consumption else False,
        "plan": getattr(consumption, "plan", None) if consumption else None,
        "subscriptionid": getattr(consumption, "subscription_id", None)
        if consumption
        else None,
        "walletbalance": getattr(consumption, "wallet_balance", None)
        if consumption
        else None,
    }


@router.post("/execute", response_model=ActionExecuteResponse)
def executeaction(request: ActionExecuteRequestModel) -> ActionExecuteResponse:
    normalized_target = request.target.strip()
    if not normalized_target:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="target must not be empty")

    # 1. Prompt injection and risk
    promptinjection = scanpromptinjectiondict(
        actiontype=request.actiontype,
        target=normalized_target,
        content=request.content,
        filepath=request.filepath,
        metadata=request.metadata,
    )

    finalriskscore = request.riskscore + int(promptinjection["riskdelta"])

    mergedmetadata = dict(request.metadata)
    mergedmetadata["promptinjection"] = promptinjection
    mergedmetadata["ownerkey"] = request.ownerkey
    mergedmetadata["requestedunits"] = request.requestedunits

    # 2. Security audit decides status
    audit = createauditevent(
        actiontype=request.actiontype,
        target=normalized_target,
        content=request.content,
        riskscore=finalriskscore,
        clientid=request.clientid,
        sessionid=request.sessionid,
        filepath=request.filepath,
        metadata=mergedmetadata,
    )

    status = _map_audit_event_to_status(audit["eventtype"])

    # If security does not allow, we never try to consume usage
    if status != "allowed":
        if status == "review":
            message = "Action requires manual review before execution."
        elif status == "quarantined":
            message = "Action has been quarantined due to elevated risk."
        else:
            message = "Action has been denied."

        return ActionExecuteResponse(
            status=status,
            actiontype=request.actiontype,
            target=normalized_target,
            ownerkey=request.ownerkey,
            requestedunits=request.requestedunits,
            finalriskscore=finalriskscore,
            promptinjection=promptinjection,
            audit=audit,
            executionallowed=False,
            usage=_empty_usage(reason="blocked_by_security_review"),
            message=message,
        )

    # 3. Security says allowed; we *attempt* usage metering but do not downgrade status
    service = get_action_execute_service()

    try:
        receipt = service.execute(
            ActionExecutionRequest(
                owner_key=request.ownerkey,
                action_name=f"{request.actiontype}:{normalized_target}",
                requested_units=request.requestedunits,
                payload={
                    "content": request.content,
                    "filepath": request.filepath,
                },
                metadata=mergedmetadata,
            )
        )
        usage = _usage_to_dict(receipt)
    except Exception:
        # Treat metering failures as non-fatal for this boundary
        return ActionExecuteResponse(
            status="allowed",
            actiontype=request.actiontype,
            target=normalized_target,
            ownerkey=request.ownerkey,
            requestedunits=request.requestedunits,
            finalriskscore=finalriskscore,
            promptinjection=promptinjection,
            audit=audit,
            executionallowed=True,
            usage=_empty_usage(reason="usage_metering_unavailable"),
            message="Action approved for execution.",
        )

    # We do not override the audit-driven status; if audit said allowed, we stay allowed
    return ActionExecuteResponse(
        status="allowed",
        actiontype=request.actiontype,
        target=normalized_target,
        ownerkey=request.ownerkey,
        requestedunits=request.requestedunits,
        finalriskscore=finalriskscore,
        promptinjection=promptinjection,
        audit=audit,
        executionallowed=True,
        usage=usage,
        message="Action approved for execution.",
    )
